title: Remove commented-out code
why: Disabled source in comments rots, obscures current behavior, and duplicates version-control history.
suggestion: Delete the disabled code and recover it from version control if it is needed later.
limitations: Recognizes likely disabled statements in real single-line slash and hash comments and reports one representative location per file. Keyword boundaries and qualified statement shapes distinguish prose from source; string contents, documentation comments, fenced examples, ASN.1 specifications, explicit API illustrations and narrated situations, formula definitions, explicitly proposed simplifications, annotation-prefixed prose, common mathematical notation, and foreign declaration syntax in Rust comments are excluded.

Unlabelled syntax illustrations can remain ambiguous. Development-only debug calls, TODO-disabled implementations, and abandoned alternatives remain reviewable rather than being exempted merely because their intent is documented.
